correctness.rationale: Rationalization gives Δₕ=h g(R/h), g(t)=c/t+O(t⁻³) for t≥1, and Δₕ/h²≤c/R. Below the moment threshold use domination by (c/R)ᵖ; above it change variables X=hy and use the integrable rescaled kernel. At p=d, the integral for h≤R≤δ has main term cᵈ h²ᵈ times the angular-density integral against dR/R. The O((h/R)²) relative kernel error, the inner ball and the exterior each contribute O(h²ᵈ) at fixed δ; continuity at zero controls the coefficient without requiring a density derivative. The stated means, variances and fourth-moment constants follow: for d≤4 the centering terms are lower order (at d=4 they are O(h⁸) versus h⁸ log(1/h)); in d≥5 use L⁴ convergence. The sample-variance identity follows from the pair kernel (Yᵢ−Yⱼ)²/2: disjoint pairs have zero covariance and overlapping pairs have covariance (μ₄−σ⁴)/4. For bounded N, κ≥1 implies a strictly positive lower bound 2/[N(N−1)]; this verifies necessity in the finite-kurtosis regime. The positive Clifford branch exists because an orthogonal Clifford generator exchanges the signs. Statistical independence of coordinates is not needed; the joint density hypothesis permits dependence. The frozen script's advertised characteristic-polynomial tests compare algebraically identical expressions, not independently computed determinants. They are unnecessary to the verified analytic calculation. No supplied code was executed.
